# 4 Ezra Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Third dialogue

---

**8:1** And he answered me and said: The Most High made this world for the sake of many, but the world to come for the sake of few.

**8:2** But I will tell you a parable, Ezra: as when you ask the earth and it says it gives much clay from which earthenware is made, but little dust from which gold comes — so also is the course of the present world.

**8:3** Many are created, but few shall be saved.

**8:4** Then I answered and said: Swallow then your understanding, O my soul, and let your heart devour wisdom.

**8:5** For without your will you came, and against your will you depart; and you have been given only a short time to live.

**8:6** O LORD above us, grant your servant to pray before you, and give us a seed for our heart and cultivation of understanding to our mind, so that fruit may come from it by which every mortal who bears the likeness of man shall be able to live.

**8:7** For you alone exist, and we are a work of your hands, as you have declared.

**8:8** And since you quicken the body that is fashioned in the womb and furnish it with members, your creation is preserved in fire and water, and nine months your workmanship endures the creature created in it.

**8:9** But that which keeps and that which is kept shall both be kept by your keeping; and when the womb delivers again what has been created in it,

**8:10** you have commanded that from the parts of the body — that is, from the breasts — milk, the fullness of the breasts, shall be supplied,

**8:11** so that what is fashioned may be nourished for a time, and afterward you direct it in your mercy.

**8:12** You have nourished it in your righteousness and disciplined it in your law, and reproved it in your wisdom.

**8:13** You will take it away in your death and let it live in your life.

**8:14** If therefore you will destroy one who with so much labor was fashioned by your command, to what purpose was he made?

**8:15** And now I will speak: concerning all mankind you know best; but I will speak concerning your people, for whom I am grieved,

**8:16** and concerning your inheritance, for whom I mourn, and concerning Israel, for whom I am sad, and concerning the seed of Jacob, for whom I am troubled:

**8:17** therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them; for I see the failures of us who dwell in the land.

**8:18** But I have heard of the swiftness of the Judge who is to come.

**8:19** Therefore hear my voice and understand my words, and I will speak before you. [This is the beginning of the words of Ezra's prayer, before he was taken up. And he said:]

**8:20** O LORD, you who inhabit eternity, whose eyes are exalted above all and look down from on high:

**8:21** whose throne is beyond all measure of thought, and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the hosts of angels stand trembling,

**8:22** and at whose bidding they are changed into wind and fire: whose word is sure and whose utterances are constant, whose commandment is strong and whose ordinance is fearful,

**8:23** whose look dries up the depths and whose indignation makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth endures forever:

**8:24** Hear, O LORD, the prayer of your servant, and give ear to the petition of your creature, and attend to my words.

**8:25** For as long as I live I will speak, and as long as I have understanding I will answer.

**8:26** O look not upon the sins of your people, but upon those who have served you in truth.

**8:27** Take no account of the endeavors of those who work wickedness, but of the endeavors of those who have kept your covenants amid afflictions.

**8:28** Think not on those who have lived wickedly in your sight; but remember those who have willingly acknowledged your fear.

**8:29** Let it not be your will to destroy those who have lived like cattle; but look upon those who have gloriously taught your law.

**8:30** Take no displeasure at those who are deemed worse than beasts; but love those who have always put their trust in your righteousness and glory.

**8:31** For we and our fathers have passed our lives in ways that bring death; but it is because of us sinners that you are called merciful.

**8:32** For if you have desire to have mercy on us who have no works of righteousness, then you shall be called merciful.

**8:33** For the righteous, who have many works laid up with you, shall out of their own deeds receive reward.

**8:34** For what is man that you should be angry with him? Or what is a corruptible race that you should be so bitter against it?

**8:35** For in truth there is no one of those born on earth who has not dealt wickedly, and among those who understand there is none who has not sinned.

**8:36** For in this, O LORD, your righteousness and your goodness shall be declared, if you are merciful to those who have no wealth of good works.

**8:37** Then he answered me and said: Some things you have spoken rightly, and according to your words it shall be.

**8:38** For indeed I will not concern myself about the creation of those who have sinned, or about their death, their judgment, or their destruction;

**8:39** but I will rejoice over the creation of the righteous, over their pilgrimage also, and the salvation and the recompense they shall receive.

**8:40** As I have spoken, therefore, so shall it be.

**8:41** For as the farmer sows many seeds in the ground and plants a multitude of seedlings, and yet not all that were sown shall come up in due season, and not all that were planted shall take root — so also those who are sown in the world shall not all be saved.

**8:42** I answered and said: If I have found grace, let me speak.

**8:43** As the farmer's seed, if it does not come up because it has not received your rain in due season, or if it has been spoiled by too much rain — so perishes the man who is formed by your hands and is called your own image, because he is made like you; for whose sake you have formed all things, and whom you have compared to the farmer's seed.

**8:44** Be not angry with us, but spare your people and have mercy upon your inheritance; for you have mercy upon your own creation.

**8:45** Then he answered me and said: The things that are present are for those who live now, and the things that are future for those who shall live hereafter.

**8:46** For you fall far short of being able to love my creation more than I love it; but you have many times likened yourself to the unrighteous.

**8:47** Let that not be so! But even in this you shall be praiseworthy before the Most High,

**8:48** because you have humbled yourself, as is fitting for you, and have not judged yourself worthy to be much glorified among the righteous.

**8:49** For many great miseries shall come upon those who in the last times dwell in the world, because they have walked in great pride.

**8:50** But understand for yourself, and seek the glory of such as are like you:

**8:51** for unto you paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is built, and rest is allowed, goodness is perfected and wisdom is perfected beforehand.

**8:52** The root of evil is sealed up from you, weakness and the moth are hidden from you, and corruption is fled into oblivion.

**8:53** Sorrows are passed away, and in the end is shown the treasure of immortality.

**8:54** Therefore ask no more questions concerning the multitude of those who perish.

**8:55** For when they had opportunity of choosing, they despised the Most High, thought scorn of his law, and forsook his ways.

**8:56** Moreover they have trodden down his righteous ones,

**8:57** and said in their heart that there is no God; though knowing full well that they must die.

**8:58** For as the things aforesaid shall receive you, so thirst and torment which are prepared shall receive them; for the Most High willed not that man should be destroyed.

**8:59** But man himself who was created defiled the name of him who made him, and was ungrateful to him who prepared life for him.

**8:60** And therefore is my judgment now at hand.

**8:61** These things I have not shown to all men, but to you and a few like you. Then I answered and said:

**8:62** Behold, O LORD, you have now shown me a multitude of the signs which you will do in the last times, but you have not shown me at what time you will do them.
